name: SOMA
scale: 1,632 human-verified questions on body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning from first-person video
created_by: Matea Tashkovska, Nael Ouerghemi, Haozhe Qi, and Alexander Mathis
release_note: The paper announces benchmark, training data, and code; downloadable artifacts were not verified.

name: ProactEgoMem
scale: 300 daily-life and 100 scientific clips; 1,500 QA items testing proactive information capture, state tracking, and location tracking
created_by: Ruotong Liao, Meikel Kokowski, and collaborators at LMU Munich, Stanford, Google, and TUM
released_by: mayhugotong on GitHub; Meikel on Hugging Face
release_note: Annotations, evaluation code, and leaderboard are available. Obtain source video separately. Benchmark data, including dev items, must not be used for training.

name: STOU
scale: Paper: 2,902 video-audio/text safety queries; gated release: 1,952 instances over 713 source clips, separating harm understanding from refusal
created_by: Yewon Han, Jisu Jeon, Suhyun Choi, Juan Yeo, Minsoo Jo, Gihoon Kim, Hyunggyu Lim, and Taesup Kim
access: Hugging Face agreement; source videos acquired separately
release_note: The public card documents a smaller gated release than the paper. Clip reconstruction instructions and annotations are listed; evaluation code is still marked coming soon.

name: EgoVoice
scale: Proactive spoken assistance from HoloAssist-derived video/audio streams, jointly evaluating speech timing and guidance content
created_by: Heeseung Kim
release_note: The project schedules code, models, and dataset for November 2026; these assets are not yet verified as released.

name: Ropedia W0
license: Apache-2.0 code; CC-BY-NC-4.0 weights; upstream model terms apply
scale: Camera-pose and skeleton-conditioned loco-manipulation world model trained with 10K human and 3K robot hours; 5B pre-trained and mid-trained checkpoints released
created_by: Tianqi Liu and collaborators; Ropedia
released_by: Ropedia on GitHub; ropedia-ai on Hugging Face
release_note: 5B inference and two checkpoints are available. A14B, benchmark-tuned checkpoints, evaluation package, and post-training code remain pending. The 13K-hour training mixture is not a separately verified full data release.

name: Xp-Teleop
scale: 27 Unitree G1 humanoid episodes, 543 action segments, and 96,064 frames with clean head RGB, keypoints, masks, calibration, and IMU
created_by: Ropedia
release_note: Teleoperation data are downloadable; the W0 evaluation-code package is a separate, pending release.
scope_note: Robot head-camera teleoperation, not human-worn capture; complements human-to-robot world-model evaluation.

name: TouchScale
scale: Current release: 100 hours, 15,324 episodes, 929 tasks, and 193 object meshes; synchronized head RGB-D, wrist RGB, and 880 tactile taxels per hand
created_by: Dayou Li and the TouchScale collaboration
release_note: The full 500-hour corpus is planned for release before November 2026; only the documented 100-hour portion is counted as available.

name: EMBER-Bench
scale: 189 recorded household tasks and 699 history-dependent questions: 548 next-action predictions and 151 causal traceback questions
created_by: Aoyang Cai, Boning Zhao, and collaborators at Tsinghua, HKU, and BAAI
released_by: ZHAOAlexGoat on GitHub; Alexzhao0605gt on Hugging Face
release_note: Benchmark media, portable catalog, and evaluation CLI are available. The maintained evaluator is not an exact reproduction of the paper's frozen leaderboard.

name: Ego-SpaCR / SpaC-MEM
scale: 620 ScanNet video sessions, 95 task-oriented conversations, and 3,100 evaluation queries for spatially grounded conversational memory
created_by: Jiazhou Liang, Liam Gallagher, Kiko Chen, David Guo, Armin Toroghi, Yifan Simon Liu, and Scott Sanner
release_note: Code and a 3,218-question annotation ZIP are available; use the 3,100 official_eval questions for the reported protocol. Obtain ScanNet separately. Free-text judging and other paper baselines are outside the released scorer.
scope_note: ScanNet-derived first-person spatial conversations, not a newly captured wearable corpus.

name: PWM / PWM-Bench
scale: 150 first-person world-model customization tasks across indoor, outdoor, and Minecraft scenes; 300 paired support/test videos and 33,750 frames
created_by: Zhexin Lou, Guancheng Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yang Zhao, and Hao Tang
released_by: AIGeeksGroup on GitHub and Hugging Face
access: Public benchmark files and code; consult upstream video and base-model terms
release_note: Support and test segments are disjoint within each scene, not a cross-scene generalization split. Reuse terms are not summarized by a single dataset license.

name: EgoExo-Next
license: Non-commercial research annotations; inherited source-image terms
scale: 2,503 human-curated four-choice questions from six ego/ego-exo sources, testing visual next-state prediction and cross-view correspondence
created_by: Yutong Li, Molin Wang, Xiaotong Li, Yanyan Fang, Daoguo Dong, and Ziyi Ye
release_note: Image options, input metadata, and answers are released. Dataset-viewer image-row counts are not benchmark question counts.

name: NextMe-800 / NextAct
scale: 795 hours from one Aria wearer across a 126-day span, with 527 recordings on 114 recording days; gaze, audio, five-level captions, and a 1,500-point NextAct benchmark
created_by: Zhaoxu Meng, Yiming Sun, Mingyuan Gao, Jiachang Zhang, Zhuhan Dai, Yipeng Du, Zheng Lian, and Jian-Qiao Zhu
access: Hugging Face research-use and privacy agreement
release_note: The card lists 8.81 TB of recordings plus captions and benchmark scripts. NextAct also uses EgoLife; one wearer's long history does not establish population diversity.

name: APM-Bench
scale: 549 sessions in 104 trajectories, with 2,719 candidate interactions for cross-session memory, current-scene perception, and adaptive response
created_by: Jianguo Huang, Jinming Liu, and collaborators
released_by: Jianguo-Huang11 on GitHub and Hugging Face
release_note: The 549 session videos are hosted; annotations and evaluation code are still being prepared. Do not treat the video upload as a complete runnable benchmark.

name: HumanVerse-500 / lambda_0
scale: Reported 500-hour wearable corpus synchronizing egocentric video with body and hand motion, used by the lambda_0 humanoid loco-manipulation policy
created_by: Chongyang Xu, Zhao Wu, Jin Chen, and collaborators
release_note: The paper promises code, models, and data; a downloadable release was not verified. First submission was September 30 despite the October arXiv identifier.

name: Ego4WAM
scale: Controlled world-action-model study separating human-robot alignment, duration, task diversity, action labels, and training-stage effects
created_by: Zhihao Sun, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, and collaborators
release_note: Paper verified; executable code and model weights were not verified.

name: IronMind
scale: Humanoid VLA pretraining on human ego video and robot data using camera-space actions; studies budgets from 250 to 10,000 hours
created_by: XPENG Robotics
release_note: The project provides the report and demonstrations; code, checkpoints, and the training corpus were not verified as downloadable.

name: EgoTSR++ / SpatialLogic-Bench
scale: Goal-conditioned progress reasoning from bidirectional state pairs, with order-robust comparisons and long-horizon failure/recovery evaluation
created_by: Xiaoda Yang, Can Wang, Yuxiang Liu, Pengfei Zhou, Jianwen Lou, and Shuicheng Yan
release_note: A distinct follow-up to EgoTSR; paper verified, runnable model and benchmark releases not verified.

name: EgoWild / EgoWild2Dex
scale: Reported 538.9 hours, 179,049 episodes, 125,961 task descriptions, and 1,282 object categories from in-the-wild head-camera manipulation
created_by: Kunyang Lin, Xutao Wen, Jingxi Lin, and collaborators
release_note: The paper announces data, models, and code. The reported corpus size is not a verified downloadable release size.

name: SlugTrails
scale: Aria recordings across three campus buildings and six floors, with CAD floor plans, survey-aligned trajectories, and single-frame, sweep, and walking-stream protocols
created_by: Yunqian Cheng and Roberto Manduchi
released_by: Head-inthe-Cloud on GitHub and Hugging Face
release_note: A downloadable package, checksums, and viewers are provided. Public video is anonymized; original unblurred VRS is not distributed.

name: XPACE
scale: Joint future-video and action modeling from heterogeneous human and robot experience, including simulated recoveries for policy improvement
created_by: Jiacheng Wei, Jerry Bai, and collaborators at XPENG Robotics
release_note: Technical report and demonstrations verified; downloadable model assets were not verified.

name: EEH-R / EventEgoHands++
license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 code; dataset request terms apply
scale: Real event-camera hand dataset with about 1M annotated frames, 85 sequences, eight participants, and 2.36 hours; accompanies an expanded synthetic N-HOT3D
created_by: Ryosei Hara, Wataru Ikeda, Masashi Hatano, and Mariko Isogawa; Keio University and JST PRESTO
access: EEH-R and N-HOT3D request forms linked from the official repository
release_note: Training, evaluation, and viewer code is public; dataset access is form-based.

name: EgoPathBench
scale: 31,852 training, 1,345 validation, and 1,111 benchmark questions for traversability, waypoint routes, and intent-conditioned paths from first-person RGB
created_by: Yang Zhao, Zhuo Chen, and Xubo Yang; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
release_note: File-based release with 36 archives and checksums; use the corrected benchmark_evalfix labels. A dataset-viewer format error does not mean the archives are unavailable.

name: HuRo
scale: Reported 630K robotized episodes and 142M frames from five human egocentric sources; aligns rendered robot observations with retargeted actions
created_by: Jinho Jeong and collaborators at RLWRLD and Yonsei University
release_note: Robotization pipeline code is available; the project does not yet provide a verified full-dataset download. Source-video rights still apply.

name: MINT / EgoPipeline
license: MIT original code; upstream models and MANO have separate terms
scale: Joint world-space camera and two-hand trajectory prediction; public checkpoint, training/inference code, EgoPipeline, and non-video annotations covering 1,021 hours
created_by: Zijie Zhu and collaborators at Wuji Technology, ShanghaiTech, Tsinghua, HKU, and Zhejiang University
released_by: wuji-technology on GitHub; ZZJAsher on Hugging Face
release_note: Source videos are not redistributed; separately licensed MANO and optional pipeline assets must be obtained from their providers. Pseudo-labels are not motion-capture ground truth.

name: TempCloze
scale: 1,521 videos from seven sources for selecting a missing middle clip; separates semantic plausibility, temporal alignment, and progression
created_by: Wenqi Pei, Henry Hengyuan Zhao, Yilai Liu, Jiahao Meng, Han Chen, Ziyu Wang, and Hongyang Du
released_by: CedricPei on GitHub; CedPei on Hugging Face
release_note: The Hugging Face package provides source identifiers and gap boundaries, not a self-contained video corpus. Obtain source footage under its own terms.
scope_note: Mixed-source benchmark centered on long-take and egocentric video; not all source footage is wearable capture.

name: AnyWorld
license: Apache-2.0 code; external model terms apply
scale: Factorizes action, camera, and embodiment to recompose unpaired human interactions into robot-native video-action experience
created_by: Cheng Chen, Jerry Bai, Jiacheng Wei, and collaborators
release_note: Image-editor training/inference and world-model inference code are public. External base components and adapted checkpoint setup follow the repository's model-weight guide.

name: EgoArgus
scale: 6,978 understanding examples over 3,719 source-derived clips and 789 intervention decisions over 311 hosted videos
created_by: NYCU NLP Lab / EgoArgus author team
released_by: NYCU-NLP-Lab on GitHub; tommytyc on Hugging Face
release_note: Annotations and evaluation code are public; understanding videos require separate source access. The repository calls itself a release draft and explicitly says reuse rights are not yet granted. Fifteen rows have out-of-option labels.

name: RealTimeVideo-Instruct-112K
license: CC-BY-4.0 annotations except ADT subset: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0
scale: 112,102 real-time QA/caption instruction samples, including 22,493 Ego4D and 6,861 Aria Digital Twin samples; queries occur when evidence first becomes visible
created_by: Joya Chen, Zeyun Zhong, and Mike Zheng Shou
release_note: Annotations only; fetch each source-video collection separately. The ADT subset has stricter non-commercial/share-alike terms.
scope_note: Mixed ego and general-video annotation corpus; only the named egocentric subsets are first-person.
derived_from: Ego4D; Aria Digital Twin; E.T. Instruct 164K; LLaVA-Video-178K; ActivityNet; QVHighlights

name: EgoDatasets
scale: Dataset-centric taxonomy of 96 resources from 2008-2026: 79 core egocentric/multiview datasets and 17 contextual exocentric datasets
created_by: Alexandros Mitsou and Evaggelos Spyrou; University of Thessaly
release_note: Open-access survey published October 16; distinguishes native anticipation support from adapted and post-hoc protocols.

name: EgoTac
scale: Predicts continuous force and binary contact directly from egocentric human video; trained on more than 5.7M image-tactile pairs and reports below 0.06 N mean in-domain force error
created_by: Wenkang Zhang, Chengbo Yuan, Zicheng Zhang, Zhengxue Cheng, and Yang Gao
release_note: The paper is public, but no official code, checkpoint, training corpus, or reuse license was linked in the arXiv record.

name: EgoGazeLite
scale: Software-only gaze-and-crop model for token-efficient wearable MLLM input with 15.7M parameters, 6.71 GFLOPs, and 21.6 ms/frame end-to-end latency on consumer accelerator hardware
created_by: Matteo Stoiber and Niels Buus Lassen
release_note: The archival WearableAI workshop paper is public, but no code, checkpoint, evaluation package, or license was linked.

name: Long-Tail Embodied Urban Navigation from In-the-Wild Videos
scale: Automatically annotates web-scale in-the-wild egocentric videos with metric trajectories and structured navigation semantics, then trains a VLA policy while exposing rare perception-motion failure modes
created_by: Bingyi Xia, Han Bao, Zhewei Chen, Hanjing Ye, Jingwen Yu, Yuhan Pang, Wenjun Xu, and Jiankun Wang
release_note: The arXiv paper is public, but no annotation pipeline, training data, implementation, checkpoint, or license was linked.

name: EgoHRV
scale: Estimates heart rate and heart-rate variability from headset gaze cameras; adding its uncertainty-aware HRV features improves the reported EgoExo4D proficiency result by 17.8%
created_by: Berken Utku Demirel and Christian Holz
release_note: The ECCV paper links an official GitHub repository, but that URL returned 404 during this audit; code, checkpoint, and license therefore remain unverified.

name: G3Ego
scale: Uses wearer gaze to prune action-scene graphs built from sparse frames, improving class-balanced action recognition and anticipation on EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO without large video-model pretraining
created_by: Marko Haralovic, Akash Ramakrishnan, and Estefania Talavera Martinez
release_note: The workshop paper is public, but no implementation, graph annotations, checkpoints, or license was linked.

name: DreamHand
scale: Repurposes a video diffusion model as a deterministic geometry encoder for continuous metric bimanual trajectories, reducing MPJPE-p by 30% on ARCTIC and 40% on HOT3D, with 46-61% gains when out-of-sight hands are counted
created_by: Yufei Liu, Xixi Wang, Hao Li, Ganlong Zhao, Kaitong Cai, Chengkai Jin, Chunxiao Liu, Jianbo Liu, Siyuan Huang, Xingang Pan, and Hongsheng Li
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no code, checkpoint, or license was available during this audit.

name: Helios 2.0
scale: Event-camera smart-glasses gesture system trained only on synthetic data, reporting more than 80% F1 for the six-channel model at 6-8 mW on a Qualcomm Hexagon DSP
created_by: Prarthana Bhattacharyya, Joshua Mitton, Ryan Page, Owen Morgan, Oliver Powell, Benjamin Menzies, Gabriel Homewood, Kemi Jacobs, Paolo Baesso, Taru Muhonen, Richard Vigars, and Louis Berridge
release_note: The revised arXiv record confirms presentation at the ECCV 2026 Event-Based Multimodal Vision Workshop; no implementation, trained model, dataset package, or license was linked.

name: Vision-Language Models for Egocentric Video
scale: Critical survey connecting egocentric VLMs across hand-object interaction, temporal reasoning, efficient clip selection, graph/object-centric reasoning, wearable assistance, and embodied AI
created_by: Mohammad Zamani and Fatemeh Ziaeetabar
release_note: The survey preprint is public; no companion bibliography, code, or structured data release was linked.

name: AlloEgo-VLM
scale: AlloEgo-View triplets and an SFT framework for resolving allocentric versus egocentric spatial-reference ambiguity, with an NVIDIA Isaac Sim object-search demonstration
created_by: Kuan-Lin Chen, Tzu-Ti Wei, Chao-Chi Liao, Yu-Chee Tseng, and Jen-Jee Chen
release_note: Implementation and processed AlloEgo-View images are public, but the repository does not declare a top-level software license and the processed images inherit restrictions from several source datasets.
scope_note: Reference-frame reasoning over general images and simulation rather than wearable first-person capture.

name: WorldRover-10M
scale: Synthetic minute-scale world explorations rendered from first-person, third-person, and 360-degree views with RGB, metric depth, camera trajectories, action signals, optical flow, and long-range 2D/3D tracks
modalities: synthetic-video; egocentric-video; exocentric-video; 360-video; depth; camera-pose; optical-flow; trajectories
created_by: Xiaojie Xu, Zhengyuan Lin, Runyi Li, Yihao Liu, Kaipeng Zhang, Yongtao Ge
release_note: The arXiv comments say code and data links will be updated, but no live engine, dataset, repository, or license was linked during this audit.
scope_note: Artist-built synthetic environments with multiple viewpoints, not real wearable capture.

name: UniWM
scale: Memory-augmented unified world model for robot navigation foresight and planning across Go Stanford, ReCon, SACSoN, SCAND, and unseen TartanDrive environments
created_by: University of Wisconsin-Madison Intelligent Systems Lab and collaborators
release_note: The ECCV paper, implementation, and Hugging Face dataset are public, but a repository-wide software/data license was not verified.
scope_note: Robot-navigation camera data rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: EATR-Stereo
scale: Routes paired head-mounted stereo evidence with embodiment-conditioned tokens for a 33-DoF humanoid, reporting 60% full-task, 100% grasp, and 80% stage success on long-horizon manipulation
created_by: Songwei Wu, Rui Zhao, Fan Yang, Zhongqiang Nie, Zhiduo Jiang, Wandong Sun, Yuwei Li, Jian Hu, Yang Liu, and Hong Liu
release_note: The paper is public, but no code, checkpoint, robot dataset, or license was linked.
scope_note: Robot head-camera stereo rather than human wearable video.

name: Hydra-0
scale: Generalist action-flow world model trained after filtering 2,202 hours of multi-embodiment video; reports 90.4% lower robot-motion error, 60.2% lower object-motion error, and r=0.96 replay correlation on RoboLab
created_by: NVIDIA, MIT, Brown University, and collaborators
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but the project marks code and model artifacts as coming soon.
scope_note: General multi-embodiment robot/human video rather than a specifically egocentric corpus.

name: DECOWAM
scale: Decouples camera ego-motion, mobile-base motion, and arm actions in a whole-body world-action model; introduces ARMDOG and reports a 21.7% action-MSE reduction with 25.95M trainable adaptation parameters
created_by: Siyuan Ma, Boshi Zhang, Yutian Zhang, Qinglian Wu, Jiaqi Zhai, Dong Wei, and Qiaojun Yu
release_note: The paper is public, but the ARMDOG dataset, implementation, checkpoints, and license were not linked.
scope_note: Moving robot-camera perception rather than human egocentric capture.

name: RoboEdit
scale: Edits human manipulation video into action-consistent robot video with aligned 3D states; the reported RoboEdit-14M corpus contains 174K paired videos, 14M frames, and seven robot embodiments
created_by: Yaowei Guo, Zeng Tao, Yuxin Jiang, Yunuo Chen, Zhiyang Dou, Yuxiang Ma, Yin Yang, Demetri Terzopoulos, Ying Jiang, and Chenfanfu Jiang
release_note: The paper is public, but no code, model, RoboEdit-14M package, or license was linked.
scope_note: General human manipulation video; a wearable first-person viewpoint is not required.

name: HOST
scale: Inference-time acquisition from one human video in 29 seconds on average, reporting 62% success across novel manipulation tasks; public code covers preprocessing, alignment, coupling, and policy training, with a 15.9 GB checkpoint
created_by: Guangyan Chen, Meiling Wang, Te Cui, Zichen Zhou, Qi Shao, Shalfun Li, Hang Su, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Mengyin Fu, Yi Yang, and Yufeng Yue
release_note: Training/preprocessing code and an MIT-licensed policy checkpoint are public. The checkpoint is trained robot-to-robot, the root code repository has no repository-wide license, and user normalization metadata is still required for evaluation.
scope_note: Human demonstration video is central, but the method is not restricted to wearable egocentric capture.

name: RoboMirror
scale: Retargeting-free video-to-humanoid locomotion from raw egocentric or third-person video, using VLM-derived motion intent to condition a diffusion policy; reports 80% lower control latency and 3.7% higher task success
created_by: Zhe Li, Boan Zhu, Yangyang Wei, Shuanghao Bai, Yuheng Ji, Yibo Peng, Tao Huang, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, S.-H. Gary Chan, Chang Xu, Cheng Chi, Jianfei Yang, and Shanghang Zhang
release_note: The revised paper is public, but no official implementation, checkpoint, evaluation data, or license was linked.
scope_note: Supports egocentric input, but targets humanoid locomotion rather than wearable-video understanding.

name: RoboLab-EgoX
scale: 4,000 simulation episodes and six hours across 28 RoboLab tasks and 99 scenes, including 632 successes and 3,368 failures with wrist-view RGB-D, two exterior RGB-D views, calibration, arm telemetry, actions, and language
modalities: robot-camera-video; exocentric-video; depth; camera-calibration; robot-actions; natural-language
created_by: DAVIAN Robotics, Voxel51, and NVIDIA RoboLab
scope_note: Robot wrist-view simulation benchmark rather than human wearable capture.

name: MERIT
scale: Simple episodic memory with four retrieval keys per 30-second clip and query-time neighbor filtering; reports 71.2 accuracy on EgoLifeQA, 71.8 on LVBench, and 77.7 on Video-MME Long with a GPT-5 backbone
created_by: Yeeun Choi, Youngbeom Yoo, Joon-Young Lee, Hyolim Kang, and Seon Joo Kim
release_note: The ECCV 2026 Oral paper and project page are public. The page's code link currently returns 404, so implementation and license remain unverified.

name: SCOUT
scale: Recovery-aware Chain-of-Tool-Thought agent for hours-to-days egocentric video, with adaptive region switching, uncertainty-prioritized UPS-GRPO, and turn-level temporal-alignment rewards
created_by: Keyang Zhong, Kuo Wang, Peng Liu, Quanlong Zheng, Junlin Xie, Zhijia Liang, Yanhao Zhang, and Guanbin Li
release_note: The paper confirms acceptance at ACM Multimedia 2026, but no code, model, training trajectories, or license is linked.

name: EgoTrack3D
scale: Modular dynamic 3D object tracker that lifts 2D masks into a global frame and reports an 11% PCL improvement over the strongest baseline on Aria Digital Twin
created_by: Jan Kulik, Bjarni Dagur Thor Karason, Yung-Hsu Yang, Boyang Sun, Marc Pollefeys, and Xi Wang
release_note: The paper is public, but no code, checkpoint, or standalone benchmark release is linked.

name: Ego-OSCAR
scale: Sub-$200 open-hardware stereo-inertial head-mounted capture design; the paper reports about 550 hours per camera, 1,462 sessions, synchronized 6-axis IMU, dense captions, calibration, and per-frame 3D hands
created_by: Gunjan Paul, Senthil Palanisamy, Satpal Singh Rathore, Pratyush Kumar Patnaik, Shubhanshu Khatana, and Abhishek Anand
release_note: The paper states that hardware, software, and data are open-sourced, but it provides no verifiable artifact URL; availability and reuse terms therefore remain on watch.

name: VideoNIG
scale: Goal-oriented navigation-instruction benchmark with 60K simulated ego-view tour videos and 37K text- or image-goal prompts, evaluated by language, spatial-consistency, and navigation-execution tests
created_by: Fangdi Li, Juncheng Liao, Changxu Cheng, Jiazhi Wang, Senda Chen, Tao Wang, and Wuyue Zhao
release_note: The work is adjacent because its first-person tours are simulator-generated navigation-agent views rather than human wearable recordings. No data or code release is linked.

name: EgoHieraLoc
scale: Unified VQL-2D/VQL-3D framework combining segmentation-guided query parsing, deformable correlation filtering, regional feedback, and geometry-semantic confidence for credible multi-view 3D estimates
created_by: Yifei Cao, Guolong Wang, Mingliang Hou, Xiya Bu, Daming Liu, and Yu Liu
release_note: The manuscript is under review and links no code, checkpoint, or evaluation package.

name: Fast-Slow ReAct ObjectNav
scale: Hierarchical zero-shot ObjectNav agent with a reactive value-map controller, coordinate-anchored semantic memory, pose-tagged first-person keyframes, and bounded VLM deliberation; reports 68.75% HM3D and 47.29% MP3D success
created_by: Zhaochen Lan, Zhi Yang, Yuxiang Fu, and Mengxiang Lin
release_note: The work is adjacent because its recalled first-person views come from a navigation robot, not a human wearer. No implementation is linked.

name: R4DSG
scale: Relative 4D scene-graph memory evaluated on 255 object questions from EgoLifeQA; reports a 6.7-point overall gain and a 12.5-point gain on when questions over EgoRAG-Text
created_by: Ke Ma, Yamin Mao, Weiming Li, Shuai Tan, Yijie Zhong, Hao Chen, Haofen Wang, and Meng Wang
release_note: The ACM Multimedia 2026 paper and project page are public. The linked GitHub repository contains the project site, not the method implementation or evaluation release.

name: CrossTracer
scale: Cross-embodiment navigation framework that proposes normalized image-plane traces and adapts them with embodiment-conditioned residuals; reports 45.68 on NaviTrace and real wheeled/legged deployment
created_by: Yao Wang, Siyuan Wang, Zhirui Sun, Wenzheng Chi, Liang Lin, Jiankun Wang, and Wenjun Xu
release_note: The work is adjacent because its egocentric observations are robot-camera views. No NaviTrace data, code, or checkpoint is linked.

name: AtlasVLA
scale: Wrist-camera VLA with persistent voxel-hashed 4D world memory and ego working-state memory; reports 9.4-point LIBERO-Long and 17.5-point real-world long-horizon gains over multi-view baselines
created_by: Guiyu Zhao, Longteng Guo, Yanghong Mei, Zilin Zhu, Yu Zhang, Bin Cao, Mingming Yu, Xingjian He, Jie Jiang, and Jing Liu
release_note: The work is adjacent because it uses a robot wrist camera rather than human wearable capture. No code or checkpoint is linked.

name: WNM-3D
scale: Continuous-VLN world navigation model conditioning future-view and action generation on 3D scene tokens reconstructed from monocular ego-view history, evaluated on GN-Bench
created_by: Yuehao Huang, Yunzi Wu, Xiaotao Zhang, Xinhai Li, Jiankun Dong, Jiajun Lv, Chi Zhang, Chenjia Bai, Yong Liu, and Xuelong Li
release_note: The work is adjacent because the egocentric history is captured by a navigation agent. No code, checkpoint, or training-data release is linked.

name: SLT 2026 SmartGlasses Challenge
scale: 106.98 hours across 714 four-channel smart-glasses audio sessions: 518 dyadic sessions totaling 44.95 hours and 196 multi-party meetings totaling 62.03 hours
created_by: Dehui Gao, Zhixian Zhao, Zhennan Lin, Yujie Liao, Yuhang Dai, Yike Zhu, Longshuai Xiao, Hui Bu, Xin Xu, Xie Chen, Shuai Wang, Liumeng Xue, Zhonghua Fu, Jun Du, Eng-Siong Chng, Jun Zhou, and Lei Xie
access: Training, development, and test data are distributed to registered challenge participants
release_note: The challenge site and evaluation toolkit are public, but audio access requires registration and the public repository does not declare a license.

name: HandEdit
scale: 300K+ egocentric clips and 200M+ human-to-robot editing instances from five source datasets, covering 26 embodiments split into 13 hand-only and 13 hand-arm configurations
created_by: Zhenjie Yang, Xingyu Jiao, Guopeng Zhong, Shuzhe Yang, Shi Che, Chao Wu, Chenyu Jiang, Dongjie Zhang, Yideng Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Muyun Jiang, Haisheng Su, Shuang Jin, Donghang Zhang, Chao Yang, Li Chen, Hongyang Li, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Xiaosong Jia, and Junchi Yan
release_note: The full Hugging Face dataset and evaluation toolkit are public. Dataset files use CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0; the GitHub repository does not currently expose a separate code license.

name: Proxemic Risk from Robot Ego Images
scale: Four-level proxemic-danger classification study comparing InternVL, Qwen-VL, and SmolVLM under three prompts and two QLoRA rounds, with a separate person-localization analysis
created_by: Vladyslava Rudas and Dmytro Kuzmenko
release_note: The work is adjacent because the images come from a robot's viewpoint rather than a human wearable camera. No image set, labels, or code is linked.

name: EgoCITE
scale: Context-augmented multi-view memory indexing and temporal-intent-aware evidence retrieval evaluated on EgoLifeQA, EgoMem, and EgoR1-Bench; reports 4.4-14.2-point gains and 36x lower cost than long-context agents
created_by: Le Zhang and Ke Sun
release_note: The paper is public, but no implementation, index release, checkpoint, or license is linked.

name: HumanoidVLN
scale: NVIDIA Isaac Sim benchmark spanning four humanoid embodiments and 933 collision-aware reference episodes, each with one fine-grained and three stylistic coarse instructions, plus a 20-episode Unitree G1 sim-to-real pilot
created_by: Quan-Dung Pham, Anh Dao, The-Anh Nguyen, Minh Nguyen-Dinh, Phuong Nam Dang, Tri Pham, Hung Tran, Bach Dao, Tuyen P. Le, Truong Nguyen, and Quan Nguyen
release_note: The work is adjacent because its first-person views are simulated humanoid observations. The authors state that code, benchmark, and data will be released upon acceptance, so artifacts are not yet public.

name: EgoPHI
scale: Joint dense contact-map and 3D force estimation from one egocentric RGB image and object geometry, trained with simulation supervision and tested on a real set from eight participants and two instrumented objects
created_by: Andela Ilic, Rachel Schuchert, Yijing Jiang, and Christian Holz
release_note: The ECCV 2026 paper is public, but the simulation pipeline, model, and eight-participant real-world evaluation set are not linked.

name: H2R-Bench
scale: Human-to-robot video-generation benchmark covering 11 models, six manipulation families, two robot embodiments, and five dimensions spanning goals, actions, contact, embodiment, and visual quality
created_by: Dingyi Rong, Yue Shi, Chaofan Ma, Jiezhang Cao, Zongrui Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Yao Mu, Guangtao Zhai, and Ning Liu
release_note: The benchmark paper is public, but evaluation instances, annotations, scripts, and license are not linked.

name: Clinical Freezing-of-Gait with Egocentric Vision
scale: At-home study of 13 participants with Parkinson's disease using synchronized egocentric video, wearable IMUs, and expert freezing-of-gait labels under leave-one-subject-out evaluation
created_by: Vayalet Stefanova, Diwas Lamsal, Margot Genbrugge, Maxim Yudayev, Christian Schlenstedt, Moran Gilat, Bart Vanrumste, and Benjamin Filtjens
release_note: The ECCV 2026 workshop paper is public, but the sensitive at-home recordings, labels, and code are not released.

name: ContactGuard
scale: Pre-contact execution monitor that predicts short-horizon visual latents under a robot policy's planned action chunk and aborts likely failures before wrist-camera contact
created_by: Gehan Zheng, Matthew Johnson-Roberson, and Weiming Zhi
release_note: The work is adjacent because it uses robot wrist and multi-view cameras rather than human wearable capture. No code or data is linked.

name: AdvDex
scale: Human-and-robot VLA framework introducing OmniShare multimodal demonstrations, a canonical SE(3) wrist plus 15-joint hand action space, and domain-adversarial embodiment alignment
created_by: Zhiyue Zhao, Jingyi Wu, Hairuo Liu, Mingyu Liu, Liyang Li, Hengdi Zhang, Tong He, and Zhengxue Cheng
release_note: The work is adjacent because the paper does not establish OmniShare as a human wearable first-person corpus. Dataset scale, files, code, and license are not publicly linked.

name: OccPlanner
scale: Pixel-goal diffusion planner conditioned on local 3D occupancy, with L3ROcc supervision reconstructed from monocular robot videos; reports 71.55% average success at 5-8 m versus 20.81% for NavDP
created_by: Binling Huang, Nianjin Ye, Xi Yang, Liang Hu, Zhou Huang, Shuang Wei, Longrui Yang, Yanchi Chen, and Lanpeng Jia
release_note: The work is adjacent because L3ROcc and OccPlanner use robot-view navigation video. No code, model, or L3ROcc release is linked.

name: HomeSafeBench
scale: VirtualHome free-exploration safety benchmark with 1,000 human-validated test tasks, 3,400 training tasks, five hazard categories, and 3,158 CueBack supervision trajectories
created_by: Jiashu Yao, Haoyu Wen, Siyuan Gao, Yuhang Guo, Zeming Liu, and Heyan Huang
release_note: The benchmark data and CueBack supervision are public under CC-BY-4.0, and the evaluation code is MIT-licensed. It is adjacent because observations are rendered agent views, not wearable recordings.

name: Point of View Robot Sociability Study
scale: Immersive-VR user study comparing allocentric, egocentric-proximal, and egocentric-distal judgments of identical robot trajectories and a communicative head-nod gesture
created_by: Subham Agrawal, Aftab Akhtar, Nils Dengler, and Maren Bennewitz
release_note: The work is adjacent because it studies simulated pedestrian viewpoints rather than providing human wearable-camera data. No study package or code is linked.

name: EgoBrain-Mini
scale: 40 participants and 1,562 action segments with synchronized first-person video, EEG, IMU, and audio; released subset excludes original raw video
created_by: University of Tokyo and Microsoft Research Asia EgoBrain team
release_note: All 40 subjects were announced on 2026-10-13. The release contains processed phase-2 video, not original raw video; IMU rates vary by subject.

name: CapMem
scale: Paper reports 75 videos totaling 33.7 hours and 1,000 human-annotated multiple-choice questions across 16 scenarios
created_by: Dingli Liang and collaborators
release_note: Paper reports the benchmark; public data and evaluation-code availability remain unverified.

name: ACE-Data-0
scale: Current public snapshot contains 30 room-scale takes, 1,617 videos, 92,095 images, calibration/motion/object/audio/tactile sidecars, 95,238 files, and about 3.61 TB; 150 hours, 17M+ frames, and 75K+ interactions remain the full-release target
tasks: human-demonstrations; hand-object-interaction; human-motion; tactile-learning; world-modeling; vla
modalities: fisheye-video; exocentric-video; full-body-mocap; hand-mocap; object-pose; audio; tactile; imu
created_by: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Beichen Wen, Runmao Yao, Yinghao Liu, and collaborators at NTU S-Lab and ACE Robotics
access: Repository files currently download without a Hugging Face gate; custom non-commercial research terms still apply
release_note: The repository now hosts a substantial 3.61 TB snapshot even though parts of the card still describe the data as unpublished. Keep partial because the current 30-take manifest is smaller than the announced 150-hour release and the card/file-state mismatch remains unresolved.

name: EgoMed-IEMIS
scale: 523 smart-glasses videos and 173,657 frames with referred-target masks across five medical imaging modalities, 12 targets, and five real-world viewing scenes
created_by: Rongjun Ge, Dongyang Wang, Heng Zhu, Zhirui Li, Yang Chen, and Yuting He
release_note: All five modality subsets and the method code are public. The card declares license: other and inherits terms from five source medical datasets without stating one unified redistribution license.

name: EventKitchen
scale: 5.5 hours from 10 participants in 13 kitchens with egocentric stereo events, synchronized RGB, depth, and IMU, plus 10,762 action segments and 13,482 object boxes
modalities: event-camera; stereo-video; rgb; depth; imu; action-labels; object-boxes
created_by: Chengming Feng, Hesam Araghi, Liming Zheng, Julien Dupeyroux, Xucong Zhang, Jan van Gemert, and Nergis Tomen
release_note: The ECCV 2026 paper and benchmark specification are public, but no dataset download, code repository, or reuse license was linked during this audit.

name: SoniSpeech
scale: 34 hours and 18,000 voiced and silent utterances with synchronized ultrasound echoes, audio, and frontal video; 5,356 unique words and full phoneme coverage
created_by: Ruidong Zhang, Jiacheng Liu, Francois Guimbretiere, and Cheng Zhang
release_note: The Cornell eCommons record and CC BY 4.0 dataset are public. The capture is eyewear-centered and frontal rather than a conventional outward-facing RGB corpus.

name: Assistant Placement Aria
scale: Synthetic and real indoor scenes with 2D images, 3D point clouds, text descriptions, and annotations for panel placement, sitting suggestion, and TV placement
created_by: Amir Belder, Goncalo Dias Pais, Refael Vivanti, Omri Carmi, Daniel DeTone, Oren Shrout, Ido Gattegno, and Ayellet Tal
release_note: The paper and ICRA 2026 record are public, but no benchmark files, evaluation code, leaderboard, or license was linked during this audit.

name: EgoAfford
scale: About 15.5K human-verified images from 2,000 generated multi-step scenes plus 102 real egocentric images across 26 tasks, with plans and role-specific affordance masks
created_by: Xinyuan Guan, Feifan Chen, Xinyu Zhan, Fu-Cheng Zhang, Cewu Lu, and Lixin Yang
release_note: The ungated data archives, EgoLens code, and model artifacts are public. The dataset declares MIT and the implementation repository declares Apache-2.0.

name: DreamTraj / MOVE
scale: MOVE provides 5,038 object-centric egocentric 6-DoF trajectories with fine-grained language; DreamTraj decodes trajectories from unrendered video-diffusion latents and reports 4.6x faster inference than generate-then-extract pipelines
created_by: Tongsheng Ding, Zhen Luo, Yixuan Yang, Boyu Wang, Luyang Xie, Jinyu Yang, and Feng Zheng
release_note: The project and repository are live, but the repository currently contains documentation rather than the implementation, trained model, or MOVE data files, and no license is declared.

name: GST-Bench
scale: Human-verified global spatial VQA derived from 6,790 minutes of synthetic video, mapping egocentric streams to unseen viewpoints and top-down scenes; the best reported zero-shot VLM scores 42.68 versus 79.08 for humans
created_by: Qifeng Zhang, Kaixiang Huang, Heng Dong, Huang Fang, Junting Chen, Junjie Zhu, Yonghang Chen, Zhiyu Zhang, and Wei Li
release_note: The paper announces GST-Bench, GST-Bench-Local, and GST-Train, but no public data, code, leaderboard, or license was linked during this audit.

name: VLAff / EgoAffordance
scale: EgoAffordance contains 204K episodes with 5.6M visual affordances and 11.6M grasp and trajectory affordances; VLAff predicts heatmaps, grasp poses, and executable trajectories
created_by: Jihoon Oh, Kento Kawaharazuka, and Kei Okada
release_note: The IROS 2026 paper and project page are public, but the page currently links only the paper; EgoAffordance data, model weights, and code are not released.

name: EgoGenesis
scale: Geometry-aware egocentric world-action simulator; adding 400 generated trajectories to 400 real trajectories raises reported OOD robot success from 77% to 84% for single-arm and 53% to 70% for dual-arm tasks
created_by: Zexuan Yan, Yuzhou Wu, Yue Ma, Zonghang He, Kaibo Yin, Xiaobing Tu, and collaborators
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no code, generated trajectories, model weights, or reuse license was linked during this audit.

name: EgoGVAE
scale: Guided variational autoencoder that reconstructs full-body meshes from head pose with one-step sampling, reporting more than 50x faster inference than diffusion-based alternatives
created_by: Jaehun Jung and Wonjun Kim
release_note: The ECCV 2026 paper is public, but no implementation, checkpoint, training data, or license was linked during this audit.

name: SmartRes
scale: Dynamic pixel-space resolution routing for Ego4D and EgoIntention grounding, reducing visual tokens by up to 67%, retaining 86.4% of full-resolution performance, and reporting up to 1.66x faster inference
created_by: Huixin Sun, Wangbo Zhao, Fanyue Wei, Qiuxia Lin, Pengzhan Sun, and Angela Yao
release_note: The paper says code will be made public, but no repository, checkpoint, or license was linked during this audit.

name: HiResNets
scale: Native Full-HD recognition architecture using foveal residual streams and log-polar read/write operations to preserve fine egocentric objects without quadratic feature-grid growth
created_by: Shivani Mall, Swarnim Jain, and Joao F. Henriques
release_note: The paper is public, but no implementation, pretrained weights, or reusable license was linked; the ICLR 2026 submission record was not an accepted main-conference paper.

name: Ego2Robot
scale: Pipeline converting curated and in-the-wild egocentric human manipulation video into 18,561 hours of robot-format data across 15 robot morphologies through retargeting, visual synthesis, and quality curation
created_by: Ye Wang, Pei Lin, Xiong-Hui Chen, Haoqi Yuan, Zhixuan Liang, and collaborators
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but the synthesized corpus, conversion pipeline, model weights, and reuse terms are not released.

name: RoboReact
scale: Agentic pipeline that generates egocentric RGB-D manipulation video from a single observation, extracts geometry-preserving keyframes, retargets them to humanoids, and refines execution through closed-loop VLM guidance
created_by: Shuliang He, Shuai Wang, Bo Yue, Junchi Teng, Changyu Wang, and Guiliang Liu
release_note: The paper is public, but no project page, code, generated skill library, model weights, or license was linked during this audit.

name: SiMDex
scale: Similarity-based mining selects about 1.49M task-relevant samples from a pool of roughly 32M egocentric human samples and raises reported dexterous-manipulation success from 47.7% to 61.1% over equal-sized random sampling
created_by: Nie Lin, Takehiko Ohkawa, Sijin Chen, Ruoshi Wen, Zhuohang Li, and collaborators
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no mining code, selected subset, checkpoint, or reusable license was linked during this audit.

name: JoyAI-RA 0.5
scale: Vision-Language-World-Action framework aligning action-free human egocentric video, simulation, and robot trajectories through latent and canonical action spaces for generalist manipulation
created_by: JoyAI-RA Team at JINGDONG Joy Future Academy (arXiv submitted by Peidong Liu)
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no training data manifest, code, checkpoint, or license was linked during this audit.

name: HOPE
scale: Hand-centric video transformer that predicts temporally evolving per-vertex hand pressure and contact by unifying tactile-glove, planar-pressure, and contact supervision
created_by: Subin Jeon, Byungjun Kim, and Hanbyul Joo
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no code, checkpoint, derived pressure labels, or reusable license was linked during this audit.

name: SERUM
scale: Hierarchical VLM pipeline extracting compact action and intent state models from 61 egocentric videos across coding, cooking, physical activity, and daily life
created_by: Andy J. Phu, James Mooney, Karin de Langis, Khanh Chi Le, and Dongyeop Kang
release_note: The paper states that demo, code, and results are public and the University of Minnesota NLP publication page lists COLM 2026, but a stable artifact repository and license were not resolved during this audit.

name: Hand-Object Interaction in the Age of Large Foundation Models
scale: First systematic survey of foundation-model priors for six hand-object interaction tasks, organizing eight geometric, semantic, and visual prior types and tracing HOI knowledge into robot learning
created_by: Weiquan Lin, Yu Deng, Shiyang Liu, Luping Xiao, Xu Tang, Junzhi Yu, Jiaolong Yang, Lei Zhang, and Xingyu Chen
release_note: The survey is public and describes a living companion repository, but no stable repository URL or reuse license was discoverable during this audit.

name: EgoTraj-Bench
scale: 36,947 processed sequences from 17 first-person robot sessions for translating noisy FPV trajectories into clean bird's-eye trajectories, with public intermediate data and annotations
created_by: Jiayi Liu, Jiaming Zhou, Ke Ye, Kun-Yu Lin, Allan Wang, and Junwei Liang
release_note: The processed and intermediate benchmark data are public under CC BY-NC 4.0. It is adjacent because its first-person view is robot-mounted rather than human wearable capture.

name: LAWM-3D
scale: 3D-aware latent-action learning from multiview human video using invariant action tokenization, geometric foundation-model alignment, and RGB-D reconstruction for robot world-model pretraining
created_by: Jiarui Yang, Jiale Zhange, Jiawei Li, Hang Guo, Wen Huang, Jinpeng Wang, Peidong Liu, and Shu-Tao Xia
release_note: The paper is public, but no code, model, data manifest, or license was linked. It is adjacent because the source human video is not specified as wearable first-person capture.

name: Omega-0
scale: Latent predictive whole-body world-action model supporting ego RGB plus exocentric RGB/depth; reports Omega-HOME with 40+ hours of synchronized household humanoid observations, motion, states, and action latents
created_by: Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Wenjie Zhang, Xichen Yuan, and collaborators
release_note: The paper is public, but Omega-HOME, code, checkpoints, and license are not linked. It is adjacent because the egocentric stream is robot-mounted rather than human wearable capture.

name: ReViV
scale: Unified feed-forward monocular egocentric 4D reconstruction of RGB, camera trajectory, gaze, body, hands, and depth; evaluated on HoloAssist, HOT3D, ARCTIC, Aria Digital Twin, TACO, and pretrained on more than 600 hours
modalities: egocentric-video; camera-pose; gaze; body-pose; hand-pose; depth
created_by: Xiaozhong Lyu, Gen Li, Zhiyin Qian, Xucong Zhang, Marc Pollefeys, and Siyu Tang
release_note: The implementation and pretrained checkpoints are public. Code is Apache-2.0; checkpoint use follows the separate non-commercial terms linked by the repository.

name: EgoRecovery
scale: Co-training framework that aligns egocentric human failure-recovery demonstrations with a corrective-intent space and a small robot-data anchor; its collection protocol yields more than 10x as much valid recovery data per hour as robot teleoperation
created_by: Zuhao Ge, Yuchen Zhou, Weitao Zhou, Minglei Li, Xinyu Li, Chao Wu, Hanwen Zhao, Haotian Wang, Zuxuan Wu, Xiaosong Jia, and Yu-Gang Jiang
release_note: The paper is public, but no project page, code, human-recovery corpus, robot data, or reusable license was linked during this audit.

name: Sidewalk Moments
scale: 61 first-person YouTube city-walk videos segmented into more than 50,000 ten-second clips with video, temporally averaged image, audio, and text representations for human-aligned urban-engagement analysis
created_by: Liu Liu, Freya Huying Tan, and Fabio Duarte
release_note: The manuscript is under review at Scientific Reports. No public clip list, annotations, extracted features, code, or dataset license was linked.

name: CRAFT Wearable Creative AI
scale: Context-aware smart-glasses creative-AI probe studied through nine writer interviews, co-design with 16 writers and researchers, and 24 real-world sessions with eight writers
created_by: Runze Cai, Yuxuan Huang, Lin-Ping Yuan, Kexin Xiang, David Hsu, Collier Nogues, Jussi Holopainen, and Shengdong Zhao
release_note: The arXiv record reports conditional PACM IMWUT acceptance pending minor revisions. No reusable prototype, study package, code, or license was linked, so the venue remains arXiv until final publication is verifiable.

name: SHARE User-Centric AR SLAM
scale: User-prioritized edge SLAM for commercial head-mounted AR and a ground robot in shared workspaces; reports 13.22 ms average AR latency, a 43.3% reduction, while maintaining sub-2-centimeter tracking
created_by: Tianyuan Du, Tianyi Hu, Hanting Ye, and Maria Gorlatova
release_note: The paper and user study are public, but no implementation, system traces, study data, or reusable license was linked.

name: EgoPlay
scale: Event-triggered egocentric video-to-video editing trained on 106K clip-prompt pairs, primarily from Ego4D, with positive, negative, and multi-event triggers plus event-aware evaluation
created_by: Jinjie Mai, Gordon Guocheng Qian, Willi Menapace, Arpit Sahni, Chaoyang Wang, Ashkan Mirzaei, Runjia Li, Sergey Tulyakov, Bernard Ghanem, Peter Wonka, and Rameen Abdal
release_note: The accepted SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 paper and project demonstrations are public. The linked benchmark repository was unavailable during this audit, and no training data, model weights, code, or reusable license could be verified.

name: Data Pyramid for Embodied Manipulation
scale: Survey and living catalog organizing real-robot, UMI, human egocentric and ego-exo, simulation, and general video data into a five-level embodied-manipulation data pyramid
created_by: Yifan Ye, Yankai Fu, Yaoxu Lv, Bohan Hou, Jun Cen, Lingdong Kong, Duo Zheng, Tianxing Chen, Jiaming Liu, Ziang Cao, Yunfan Lou, Wei Chow, Xian Sun, Yingshuo Wang, Kuangzhi Ge, Xiaowei Chi, Xidong Zhang, Zhibo Pang, Yiwu Zhong, Sirui Han, Zhihe Lu, Weihao Yuan, Qifeng Chen, Michael Yu Wang, Yao Mu, Ziwei Liu, Jianfei Yang, Ping Luo, and Shanghang Zhang
scope_note: Broad embodied-manipulation survey in which egocentric and UMI resources are one major layer rather than the exclusive subject.

name: HiFi-UMI-2K
scale: 2,000 hours of public robot-free manipulation demonstrations from a high-fidelity UMI rig with head stereo-inertial SLAM, native inter-gripper pose, microsecond GPIO synchronization, and two roughly 200-degree cameras per hand; reports 3 mm local end-effector accuracy
modalities: egocentric-video; stereo-video; wrist-video; camera-pose; gripper-pose; imu; robot-actions
created_by: Simple AI; Yuteng Wei, Jinming Ma, Jiawei Wang, Weitao Zhou, Yushen Zuo, Ke Rui, Minglei Li, Jinhao Zhang, Zhikang Pan, Xiang Wang, Haoran Jia, Huan Du, Zicheng Zeng, Jun Ma, Guiyu Qin, Di Zhang, and Xiaofei Li
release_note: The ungated Hugging Face release is public under CC-BY-4.0. The paper distinguishes this 2,000-hour release from the larger internal corpus used in some experiments.

name: EgoSafe-Bench
scale: 12,000 safety-reasoning evaluation samples formed from 3,000 first-person mobile-captured clips and hierarchical QA chains spanning evidence anchoring, blind-spot deduction, intent inference, and causal consistency
created_by: Yuyun Chen, Tianao Li, TianQuan Feng, Cen Chen, Huiping Zhuang, Hao Peng, and Ziqian Zeng
release_note: The paper describes a new benchmark, but no public clips, annotations, evaluation code, project page, or license was linked.

name: HumanCLAW-Bench
scale: 1,218 long-horizon egocentric find-navigate-interact episodes across 41 indoor scenes, evaluating nine VLMs through atomic full-body skill commands; the best reported success rate is 16.8%
created_by: Siyao Li, Jiawei Gu, Shuai Liu, Kairui Hu, Zekun Li, Linjie Li, Chengcheng Tang, Po-Chen Wu, Ivan Shugurov, Lingni Ma, Michael Zollhoefer, Sizhe An, Abhay Mittal, Amy Zhao, Ranjay Krishna, Manling Li, Ziwei Liu, and Chuan Guo
release_note: The project and placeholder repository are public, but the repository says the code, benchmark, weights, and environment are still being prepared and declares no license.

name: ChildLens
scale: 109 hours of vest-mounted 140-degree egocentric video and audio from 62 children aged 3 to 5 in their homes, with five location classes and 14 exhaustively annotated activity classes
created_by: Nele-Pauline Suffo, Pierre-Etienne Martin, Anas Suffo, Daniel Haun, and Manuel Bohn
access: researcher request and privacy review through the Max Planck Institute
release_note: The version of record and benchmark code are public. The child home recordings are available for research through DOI 10.17617/4.fe after a reviewed access request.

name: HuMI
scale: Portable robot-free whole-body demonstration interface and seven-dataset Hugging Face collection spanning five kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual tasks; reports 3x collection efficiency and 70% unseen-environment success
created_by: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai, Zunhao Chen, Yihang Hu, Yingdong Hu, Tong Zhang, Chuan Wen, and Yang Gao
release_note: The MIT implementation and seven public Hugging Face data repositories are live. Dataset cards declare CC-BY-4.0.

name: ContactFlow
scale: Embodiment-agnostic video action conditioning through trajectories of 3D actor-object contact points, trained with human and robot interactions and evaluated on DROID and real tabletop tasks
created_by: Sami Azirar, Enrico Pallotta, Jan Nogga, Jurgen Gall, Sven Behnke, and Hermann Blum
release_note: The paper is public, but no project page, implementation, model weights, training package, or reusable license was linked.
scope_note: Uses general human interaction and robot videos; human wearable or first-person capture is not required.

name: Robot-Factored World Models
scale: Action-conditioned world model that factors robot control and appearance into nominal trajectories and rendered robot geometry, evaluated on DROID and egocentric RoboCasa-GR1 with zero-shot embodiments and human-demo retargeting
created_by: Byungjun Kim, Taeksoo Kim, Hyunsoo Cha, and Hanbyul Joo
release_note: The project and repository are public, but the repository still says code coming soon and declares no license.
scope_note: Robot-camera world model with an egocentric humanoid evaluation, not a human wearable-capture resource.

name: EgoExoMoCap
scale: Distributed human-motion capture in which two or more people wear smart glasses; fuses head and optional wrist tracking with DINOv3 image features and is evaluated on two in-the-wild ego-exo datasets
created_by: Jiaxi Jiang, Bharat Lal Bhatnagar, Nan Yang, Lingni Ma, Sebastian Starke, Robin Kips, Nadine Bertsch, Christian Holz, and Federica Bogo
release_note: The ECCV 2026 paper is public. Its arXiv-linked project and code URL returned 404 during this audit, so no implementation or reusable license could be verified.

name: Exo2EgoPose
scale: Vision-language-guided egocentric 3D hand-pose forecasting that reconstructs exocentric demonstrations to guide ego-view prediction, evaluated on AssemblyHands, Ego-Exo4D, EgoMe-pose, and CALVIN transfer
created_by: Zhaofeng Shi, Heqian Qiu, Lanxiao Wang, Xiang Li, and Hongliang Li
release_note: The ACM MM 2026 paper states that code will be released, but no public implementation, checkpoint, or license was available during this audit.

name: Let the Body Follow
scale: Coupled egocentric whole-body teleoperation for TIAGo in which head and arm motion automatically coordinate torso and mobile-base control; evaluated in a home-care-inspired user study
created_by: Tsung-Chi Lin, Yichen Xie, and Chien-Ming Huang
release_note: The work is submitted to Humanoids 2026, not listed as accepted. No public code, hardware package, study data, or license was found.

name: VideoTreeSearch
scale: Self-correcting temporal-tree search agent for grounded long-video QA, with SFT and RL code, an 8B checkpoint, and released trajectories/evaluation data; gains 7.4 T-F1 on Haystack-Ego4D
created_by: Ce Zhang, Ziyang Wang, Yulu Pan, Oluwatumininu Oguntola, Pranav Wagh, Qiyu Wu, Hiromi Wakaki, Mohit Bansal, and Gedas Bertasius
release_note: The MIT-licensed repository includes inference, SFT, and RL implementations. Hugging Face hosts the trained checkpoint and metadata/trajectory package; source videos retain their original access rules and are not redistributed.

name: EgoPoseVR
scale: 18,235 synthetic 100-frame RGB-D/HMD motion clips across seven VR scenes, derived from 2,344 AMASS sequences and split 14,702/1,827/1,706 for train/validation/test; 388 GB on Hugging Face
created_by: Haojie Cheng, Shaun Jing Heng Ong, Shaoyu Cai, Aiden Tat Yang Koh, Fuxi Ouyang, and Eng Tat Khoo
release_note: The ungated 388 GB package contains paired RGB-D observations, HMD signals, SMPL parameters, and pose labels under CC-BY-4.0. The work is listed for IEEE VR 2026 and IEEE TVCG.

name: EgoMonth
scale: 300+ hours of first-person daily-life recordings from 20 participants spanning 20-120 days, with 1,443 human-crafted multiple-choice questions across 14 tasks; the 93.2 GB public repository includes annotations, scripts, and eight sample videos
created_by: Weitao Chen, Hu Jiaxin, Xie Tianyidan, Yang Li, Yuyi Qian, Banghao Xu, Ziheng Tang, Shenyi Wang, Mingyue Yu, Duo Li, Jiacheng Shi, Gao Wang, Zhan Xu, Zhicheng Qiu, Xuanfu Li, Jian Yang, Lanjun Wang, and Zili Yi
release_note: The de-anonymized paper now documents the full cohort and 14-task benchmark. The repository exposes annotations, evaluation scripts, and eight sample videos; full raw video uses controlled research access, and the card's CC-BY-NC-4.0 tag conflicts with its research-only license file.

name: EgoObjects-Camera
scale: Public 508 MB annotation release with predicted roll, pitch, vertical field of view, radial distortion, and parse validity for 241,554 EgoObjects images across 49 shards
created_by: Kang Liao and Puffin collaborators; derived from EgoObjects
release_note: All 49 annotation shards and the Puffin captioning pipeline are public, but neither the Hub dataset nor its README declares reuse terms for the derived annotations.

name: Think at 5 Hz, Act at 20 Hz
scale: Asynchronous driving VLA with a frozen 7B slow reasoner and fast action expert, producing fresh control every 50 ms and raising CARLA LangAuto-Short route completion from 37.0 to 94.0
created_by: Yun Li, Jiachen Gong, Simon Thompson, Ehsan Javanmardi, Qunli Zhang, Zifan Zeng, Shiming Liu, Peng Wang, Zixuan Guo, and Manabu Tsukada
release_note: The arXiv paper is public, but no code, checkpoint, training data, or license was linked.
scope_note: Autonomous-driving camera input rather than human or animal wearable first-person capture.

name: IMBench
scale: Intuitive-manipulation benchmark spanning 35 tasks, seven categories, and 14K filtered trajectories, jointly testing perception, physical reasoning, action generation, and iterative execution
created_by: Anurag Maurya, Sukhvansh Jain, Prajwal Avhad, Gautham Balachandran, Ziyi Zhou, Atharva Kshirsagar, Satyam Singh, Bowen Li, Rishabh Mukund, Ritul Singh, Jatin Vira, Suvonil Chatterjee, Devesh K. Jha
release_note: The project and Apache-2.0 Hugging Face organization expose the aggregate benchmark plus per-task datasets for all 35 tasks.
scope_note: Robot-manipulation benchmark rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: AC-VLA
scale: Plug-and-play compositional VLA training with instruction decomposition, trajectory alignment, and state-conditioned wrist-view masking; reports about 28% absolute improvement on LIBERO compositional OOD tasks
created_by: Xiaojiang Peng, Kai Peng, Jie Lu, Zheng Lian, Zitong Yu, and Xiaobo Wang
release_note: The arXiv paper is public, but no implementation, checkpoint, processed supervision, or license was linked.
scope_note: Robot VLA method evaluated on LIBERO rather than a human wearable resource.

name: SkillNav
scale: Training-free object-goal navigation framework that writes composable behavioral skills into a curiosity-value map, reaching SPL 25.5 on MP3D and 43.2 on HM3D v0.2
created_by: Ruijie Sang, Yiqun Duan, Pinhan Fu, Ruilin Wang, Wei Sui, and Xianda Guo
release_note: The arXiv paper is public, but no source code, evaluation package, or license was linked.
scope_note: Robot object-goal navigation from agent camera observations, not human wearable capture.

name: Orbis 2
scale: Hierarchical driving world model separating long-horizon coarse structure from detailed generation and combining diffusion-forcing pretraining with teacher-forcing fine-tuning
created_by: Sudhanshu Mittal, Arian Mousakhan, Silvio Galesso, Karim Farid, Jonannes Dienert, Rajat Sahay, and Thomas Brox
release_note: The project page provides results and videos but currently labels the code, model, and demo as coming soon; no reusable artifact or license is available yet.
scope_note: Autonomous-driving world model rather than human or animal wearable first-person capture.

name: Data and Learning Where it Matters
scale: Targeted autonomous data collection and offline RL for contact-critical task segments, combined with conventional free-space planning; averages 96% success across four real tasks using 2 to 2.5 hours of data
created_by: Oliver Hausdorfer, Linus Schwarz, Gabor Marko, Christian Dietz, Timo Class, Luka Hofer, Jim Yun-Jin Li, Johannes Hechtl, Ralf Romer, and Angela P. Schoellig
release_note: The paper and anonymous project page are public, but no stable code/data release or license was verified.
scope_note: Robot contact-rich manipulation rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: MotionForesight
scale: Repurposes frozen video-prediction and 3D-tracking priors to forecast future object-centered 3D scene flow from short monocular human-object video context, trained on 40K videos
created_by: Homanga Bharadhwaj and Yash Jangir
release_note: The project page provides visual results, but no public implementation, weights, training set, or license was found.
scope_note: General monocular human-object videos; wearable first-person capture is not a stated requirement.

name: Ego Scene Augmentation (ESA)
scale: Ego-element Graph framework that combines visual-foundation-model signals into an explicit egocentric spatial representation, improving EgoTextVQA by 8.14% indoors and 8.72% outdoors
created_by: Chi Kit Wong, Ye Pan, Yuanhuiyi Lyu, Xu Zheng, Zidong Cao, Lutao Jiang, Zixin Zhang, Huiyu Zhou, and Xuming Hu
release_note: The public repository contains inference scripts, graph construction code, prompts, EgoTextVQA support files, and results, but it does not declare a software license or release a trained checkpoint.

name: VIABench
scale: 761 first-person videos, 46.9 hours, and 14,526 annotations for proactive reminders, assistive QA, and vision-guided interaction
created_by: Yunfeng Liu, Yuandong Yang, Jiarui Han, Zhenpeng Huang, Yuqing Tang, Xiangyu Zeng, Gangshan Wu, and Limin Wang
released_by: MCG-NJU on GitHub and Hugging Face
release_note: The official Hugging Face dataset is live (about 69.3 GB). The linked GitHub repository remains README/assets-only; a complete runnable evaluator was not verified. Consult source-video terms rather than assuming a repository license covers every recording.

name: EgoWearBench / Wearable AI Dataset
scale: 700 validation samples per task across EgoConv conversational QA, EgoLongQA long-video QA, and EgoProactive streaming assistance; includes an evaluation starter kit
created_by: Meta AI and the ECCV 2026 Wearable AI Workshop
access: automatic Hugging Face agreement requiring contact-information sharing
release_note: Official card now names the package EgoWearBench. The three 700-sample configurations and starter kit are gated by a Hugging Face agreement; sample counts should not be read as unique-video counts across tasks.

name: HUI360
scale: 99 in-the-wild robot-mounted 360-degree HRI recordings, with a 1M-annotation HUI360 open set and 6M released SSUP-HRI annotations covering 2D pose, facial keypoints, masks, tracking, and interactions
created_by: Raphael Lorenzo-Louis, Fabio Amadio, Bertrand Luvison, and Serena Ivaldi
release_note: The FG 2026 paper (arXiv:2608.11051) confirms capture from a mobile robot, so HUI360 is adjacent rather than human-wearable egocentric data. Processed annotations and baselines are public; raw panoptic images are available on research request under GDPR, and no unified data license is declared.

name: EgoDyn-Bench
scale: 1,000 three-second clips (500 nuScenes and 500 CARLA/Cosmos-transferred), 14 question types and about 14,000 oracle-labelled QA pairs, per-clip dynamics arrays, and a 49-model reference leaderboard
created_by: TUM Autonomous Vehicle Systems
release_note: The 1.16 GB benchmark is public. The bundle is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, CARLA-derived artifacts are CC-BY-4.0, and the code is Apache-2.0.
scope_note: Autonomous-driving ego-motion video rather than human or animal wearable first-person capture.

name: VTM-Nav
scale: Training-free cross-episode object-goal navigation with persistent room- and object-level visual-topological memory, coarse-to-fine retrieval, and a conservative execution guard, evaluated on HM3D v0.1/v0.2 and MP3D
created_by: Xiaoran Xu, Yupeng Wu, Tianyu Xue, Yifan Xu, Xuanran Dong, Xiaoshan Yang, and Changsheng Xu
release_note: The arXiv record links no implementation, checkpoint, benchmark package, or license.
scope_note: Robot-agent navigation memory rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: SafeRelBench
scale: 507 executable household-agent evaluations, including 248 spatial-relation safety cases and 259 controls, testing whether VLM-driven agents satisfy support, containment, and proximity constraints before risk-prone actions
created_by: Huaigang Yang, Ya Li, Min Ren, Bo Dai, Zhenliang Zhang, and Zhaofeng He
release_note: The preprint provides no benchmark files, simulator configuration, evaluation code, or license.
scope_note: Household robot-agent safety evaluation rather than human wearable capture.

name: SoftNav
scale: Injects one continuous 3D soft token per detected object or frontier into a frozen VLM using about 1,200 samples and 17M trainable parameters, with transfer across HM3D-OVON, GOAT-Bench, SG3D, and a real robot
created_by: Yi Wu, Junjie An, Xiao Liu, Yiqun Zhou, Yuechen Wu, Xiaoqing Guan, Shuyang Yu, You Wang, and Guang Li
release_note: IROS 2026 acceptance is stated in the arXiv record, but no code, checkpoint, training sample, or license is linked.
scope_note: Robot object-goal navigation rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding
scale: Latent Tactile Predictor grounded at intermediate action-expert features, selected through linear probing to align VLA representations with future contact consequences without predicting noisy raw tactile signals
created_by: Ruilin Chen, Jingkai Jia, Tong Yang, Xinyu Zhou, Qiao Sun, Jiangwei Zhong, Shizeng Zhang, Nuo Chen, Bailin He, Wei Li, and Wenqiang Zhang
release_note: The arXiv record provides no code, checkpoint, tactile dataset, or license.
scope_note: Robot tactile-VLA method rather than human wearable capture.

name: Action QFormer
scale: Instruction-conditioned query interface that reorganizes inherited multimodal features before action generation, raising zero-shot sim-to-real navigation success from 18.8% to 56.3% and action correctness from 22.5% to 75.5%
created_by: Yufeng Ji, Wenhao Tang, Haoyi Niu, Koushil Sreenath, Yi Wu, and Zhongyu Li
release_note: The arXiv record links no implementation, checkpoint, evaluation package, or license.
scope_note: Robot navigation VLA architecture rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: Reflex
scale: Streaming flow-matching VLA inference with static/sliding/dynamic attention regions, AdaRMSNorm, asynchronous visual encoding, and operator fusion, reporting 2.58x speedup, stable 50 Hz control, and up to 54% lower reaction latency
created_by: Yuanchun Guo and Bingyan Liu
release_note: ICML 2026 acceptance is stated by the arXiv record, but no runtime, code, checkpoint, or license is linked.
scope_note: Robot VLA inference framework rather than human wearable capture.

name: FoMoVLA
scale: Couples compact future-feature foresight with sparse 2D point trajectories through future-conditioned cross-attention, supplying both target-state and motion-path supervision for continuous VLA policies
created_by: Wei Li, Peijin Jia, Yuan Ma, Xuefeng Jiang, Titong Jiang, Sheng Sun, Yujian Li, Xin Wen, Han Hong, Zhikang Liu, Bailin Li, and Kun Zhan
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but no code, checkpoint, training data, or license is linked.
scope_note: Robot manipulation VLA method rather than human wearable capture.

name: LifelongVLA
scale: Dual-timescale LoRA gating separates short-term plasticity from long-term consolidation, paired with cache-efficient stochastic replay for sequentially expanding manipulation skills on an xArm robot
created_by: Yao He, Gan Sun, Wenqi Liang, Fazeng Li, Yang Cong
release_note: The arXiv record provides no implementation, checkpoint, replay cache, evaluation trajectories, or license.
scope_note: Robot lifelong-learning VLA method rather than human wearable capture.

name: Steering Robustness into World Action Models
scale: Mechanistic analysis of robustness-relevant WAM activations plus contrastive steering directions and a reduced-order World-Action LQR controller, improving robustness on Cosmos-Policy and DiT4DiT
created_by: Jihoon Hong, Julian Skifstad, Qiyue Dai, Alice Chan, and Glen Chou
release_note: The arXiv record links no steering implementation, checkpoints, evaluation rollouts, or license.
scope_note: Robot WAM robustness method rather than human wearable capture.

name: AeroAct
scale: First reported real-world aerial WAM, adapting a video diffusion Transformer to predict local quadrotor trajectory-action chunks from egocentric visual history, proprioception, and language without decoding future video at deployment
created_by: Xinhong Zhang, Qiyuan Zhu, Yubo Huang, Haolin Chen, Runqing Wang, Yuhao Mo, Zhongxin Chen, Yu Hu, Xinjiang Wang, Jian Sun, and Gang Wang
release_note: The arXiv record provides no implementation, flight dataset, checkpoint, or license.
scope_note: Quadrotor onboard video and control rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: DriftWorld
scale: Single-forward-pass action-conditioned world model generating robot future frames at more than 30 fps, reported 17x faster on average than diffusion baselines and reaching up to 0.99 correlation for offline policy ranking
created_by: Susie Lu, Haonan Chen, Weirui Ye, and Yilun Du
release_note: The official project and GitHub repository are public, but the repository currently contains only a README and assets; implementation, checkpoints, and a license are absent.
scope_note: Robot world-model planning and policy evaluation rather than human wearable capture.

name: BadWAM
scale: World-Action Drift Attack framework testing action-only and imagination-preserving perturbations; the reported action-only attack lowers one WAM from 96.5% to 43.1% closed-loop success
created_by: Qi Li, Xingyi Yang, and Xinchao Wang
release_note: The arXiv record links no attack code, evaluation package, adversarial examples, or license.
scope_note: Robot WAM security evaluation rather than human wearable capture.

name: RoboTTT
scale: Test-time-training robot policy scaling visuomotor context to 8K timesteps without growing inference latency, enabling one-shot imitation from a human video, online improvement, perturbation recovery, and a five-minute ten-stage assembly
created_by: NVIDIA GEAR, Stanford University, and The University of Texas at Austin
release_note: The NVIDIA project page provides the paper, full rollout videos, architecture details, and evaluations, but no code, model weights, training data, or license.
scope_note: Robot policy research using a human video as context rather than releasing a human wearable-video resource.

name: EgoProceVQA
scale: 1,272 source clips and 3,600 key-step question-answer pairs across 31 procedural tasks and four scenarios, covering six question types plus the EgoProceGen data platform and self-skill-exploring EgoProceAgent
created_by: Junlong Li, Junxi Li, Yuxiang Yang, Wenbin Zou, Lap-Pui Chau, and Yi Wang
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but the benchmark-data and code buttons remain placeholders and the page says those assets will be released. The 3,600 figure counts QA pairs, not video clips.

name: EgoHTR
scale: 55 scene-aligned 4D human-motion sequences across seven challenging terrains, totaling 1.37 hours and about 150K frames from eight participants, with 36 multiview sequences and 0.7 hours of motion-capture ground truth
created_by: Alex Brandes, Haig Conti Georges Sajelian, Manthan Patel, Dominik Hollidt, Chenhao Li, and collaborators
released_by: leggedrobotics / ETH Zurich on Hugging Face
access: Hugging Face agreement with privacy, attribution, and removal conditions
release_note: The 719 GB dataset is hosted behind a Hugging Face agreement. The project still labels code coming soon; data availability does not imply the reconstruction pipeline is released.

name: Open-AoE
license: Open-AoE Dataset License; separate MANO terms for derived geometry
scale: Full approximately 2,000-hour smartphone first-person release, with 3-hour nano and 100-hour tiny subsets, camera trajectories, MANO reconstructions, and atomic actions
created_by: Ant Research / Open-AoE collaboration
release_note: The October 17 log confirms all approximately 2,000 hours uploaded. Custom dataset terms permit attributed research/commercial use; MANO-derived files have additional restrictions. Apache-2.0 applies to code, not the dataset.

name: HRIBench (Interaction-Centric VLA)
scale: 13 executable role-conditioned collaboration tasks and 650+ episodes across Instructor, Collaborator, and Intruder roles, with synchronization, responsiveness, protocol, and safety metrics; simulation adaptation raises physical GR00T N1.5 success from 0.10 to 0.43
created_by: Chang Liu, Jiawei Zhang, Tao Zhang, Ye Wang, Hongyu Zhou, and Qin Jin
release_note: The arXiv record provides no public implementation, benchmark package, simulator assets, evaluation episodes, or license.
scope_note: Human-robot collaboration benchmark built around robot observations rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: JITOMA / JITOMA-Bench
scale: Just-in-time scene-graph and memory activation for long-horizon robots, using dormant anchors and task-triggered local captioning to reduce active graph size and latency while sustaining multi-task reasoning
created_by: Yue Chang, Rufeng Chen, Yifan Tian, Dazhi Huang, Zhaofan Zhang, and collaborators
release_note: The arXiv record provides no project page, benchmark package, code, checkpoint, or license.
scope_note: Robot scene-graph memory and navigation rather than human wearable video.

name: REAL / REAL-Bench
scale: Open-world mobile-manipulation framework and 241-task REAL-Bench spanning exploration, distractors, articulated manipulation, and user disambiguation; reports 56.9% interactive success and 78.3% over 60 physical dual-arm mobile-robot episodes
created_by: Boyu Mi, Mengchen Ma, Yifei Yao, Xing Gao, Junting Chen, and collaborators
release_note: ECCV 2026 acceptance is recorded by the paper. MIT code and the ungated 3.92 GB REAL-Data package are public; the dataset is separately licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, while the checkpoint remains coming soon.
scope_note: Robot-only mobile-manipulation framework and benchmark rather than human wearable capture.

name: VSI-Super-Wild
scale: 6,980 human-verified spatial QA pairs over 442 continuous panoramic in-the-wild videos totaling 284.52 hours across eight scene categories, including recordings longer than four hours and four observer-object-environment task families
created_by: Tianjun Gu, Tianyu Xin, Kuan Zhang, Bowen Yang, Kok-Chung Chua, and collaborators
release_note: ECCV 2026 code and a public 2.67 TB dataset are live. MIT covers the repository code, but the Hugging Face dataset card does not state data reuse terms, so the release remains partial.
scope_note: Panoramic YouTube-derived long video rather than wearer-captured egocentric data.

name: Anchor-Align
scale: VLA finetuning with frozen vision-language representation anchoring and language-action alignment, improving physical xArm7 success from 28% to 54% and from 37% to 60% across two VLA architectures
created_by: Dwip Dalal, Shivansh Patel, Chahit Jain, Jeonghwan Kim, Utkarsh Mishra, and collaborators
release_note: The paper and project page are public, but the linked GitHub repository currently returns 404 and no checkpoint, data package, or license is available.
scope_note: Robot-camera VLA finetuning rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: GPUSimBench
scale: Benchmark for GPU robot simulators covering inclined-plane real-to-sim physical consistency, throughput and memory scaling, plus run-to-run and inter-environment nondeterminism in Isaac Lab and Genesis
created_by: Huzhenyu Zhang, Shenghai Yuan, Wenrui Yan, Li Ma, Hengjie Li, Jingcheng Pang, and Dmitry Yudin
release_note: IROS 2026 publication status is confirmed by the authors' official publication page, but no benchmark code, experiment package, or license is linked.
scope_note: Robot-simulator infrastructure benchmark without human wearable capture.

name: WANDA / Worlds in One Demo
scale: Synthetic-data engine expanding one real demonstration per task into 16,922 LeRobot episodes and about 26.8M timesteps (roughly 248 hours at 30 fps) across five long-horizon mobile-manipulation tasks and diverse generated worlds
created_by: Lingxiao Guo, Huanyu Li, and Guanya Shi
release_note: The 16,922-episode Hugging Face package is public under CC-BY-4.0. The project marks source code as coming soon.
scope_note: Synthetic robot mobile-manipulation trajectories rather than human wearable video.

name: Reverse to Advance
scale: Learns difficult manipulation policies by collecting easier reverse-direction rollouts, temporally inverting and filtering them with kinematic and critic priors, then iterating hard-task policy training with automated reset cycles
created_by: Qiyuan Qiao, Ge Yuan, Can Wang, and Dong Xu
release_note: The arXiv record provides no project page, implementation, checkpoints, trajectory data, or license.
scope_note: Robot manipulation data-collection method rather than human wearable capture.

name: JOP-VLN
scale: Three-stage VLN training that combines imitation learning, DAgger recovery trajectories, and on-policy reinforcement learning, reaching 69.9% success on R2R and 68.0% on RxR
created_by: Qingrong He, Lin Zhao, Kevin Zheng, and Liang Lin
release_note: IROS 2026 status is stated by the official project page, but no public code, checkpoint, training trajectories, or license is linked.
scope_note: Navigation-agent observations rather than human wearable first-person capture.

name: UESF-Bench / SeekFollow-VLA
